newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude strengthens, uptrend seen intact.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude strengthens, uptrend seen intact.

text.p: North Sea Brent trade was quiet on Friday but spot and paper markets strengthened in late business, buoyed by firmer benchmark IPE crude futures, traders said.
They said talk of a possible conclusion to the French truckers' strike which has dulled demand from French refiners and the keeping of all five Brent dates turning wet today were also supportive.
No new deals were reported on either the North Sea physical market or the forward paper market.
But short dated CFD contracts were more actively traded as players sought to cover against any volatility when the NYMEX market reopens on Monday after two days of holidays for Thanksgiving.

Next week's dates traded at Jan Brent +23 up to Jan Brent +26 cents, giving some indication that traders expected the market to hold steady although they said initially there may be some softening next week as NYMEX play's catch-up to this week's narrow falls. However, most traders agreed the markets uptrend continued to look intact with most grades looking tight through December, with scarce Urals supply continuing to draw North Sea barrels.
"There has been nothing traded in the Med yesterday or today but then there is not much on offer," a Med trader said, referring to delays at Russia's main oil port of Novorossiisk.
He said refiners would value Urals at a 20 cent discount to Dated Brent, which would make Iraqi crude when it appears on the market very competitive.
